title: CTE Mismatch Fatigue and Creep in Solder Joints
introduction: Photovoltaic module solder interconnects bond materials with substantially different coefficients of thermal expansion: silicon cells, glass, copper ribbons, and solder alloys all expand and contract at different rates during thermal cycling. Each temperature excursion imposes a thermo-mechanical stress cycle on the solder joint. Over thousands of daily field cycles, these repeated stresses produce two forms of damage — cyclic fatigue crack nucleation and growth, and time-dependent creep deformation that accumulates in the solder alloy whenever temperatures are elevated. Both damage modes progressively degrade the solder joint and can ultimately cause electrical open-circuit failure.
reasoning: The 1261-MDPI study documents CTE mismatch among silicon, glass, copper, and solder as the thermo-mechanical stress source driving both fatigue cracks and creep damage in PV solder joints under real field thermal cycling.

key_findings.claim: CTE mismatch among silicon, glass, copper, and solder generates thermo-mechanical stress during each thermal cycle
key_findings.detail: The constituent materials bonded in a PV module solder joint — silicon, glass, copper, silver, solder, and intermetallic compounds — have significantly different thermal expansion coefficients. [^mdpi1261a] When temperature changes, the CTE mismatch between these bonded materials generates thermo-mechanical stress that is applied to the solder joint on every temperature cycle. [^mdpi1261b]

key_findings.claim: Cyclic thermo-mechanical stress develops microcracks in solder joints that can spread to cause open-circuit failure
key_findings.detail: The repeated cyclic loading from CTE mismatch produces microcracks in the solder interconnection as one of the results of solder joint deterioration. [^mdpi1261c] If a fatigue crack spreads across the entire solder joint region, the result is an open circuit. [^mdpi1261d]

source_locations.quote: The development of microcracks is one of the results of solder joint deterioration.
An open circuit will result if a crack spreads across the entire joint region.

key_findings.claim: Solder creep deformation accumulates during elevated-temperature phases of cycling and is a key life-prediction parameter
key_findings.detail: When solder temperature rises during the thermal cycle, the material creeps under the applied thermo-mechanical stress. [^mdpi1261e] This creep deformation accumulates with each cycle; the accumulated creep strain remains one of the key life-prediction parameters for assessing solder joint reliability under field thermal cycling. [^mdpi1261f]
